newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: TVNZ may sell Clear shares to up Sky stake - paper.
newsitem.headline: TVNZ may sell Clear shares to up Sky stake - paper.

text.p: Television New Zealand has approached the government with a proposal to sell down its stake in Clear Communications and use the proceeds to raise its shareholding in Sky Television, the Independent Business Weekly reported on Friday.
The paper said the network had confirmed the approach to government, but said selling Clear was only one of several options to fund a possible expansion into Sky.
"No decisions have been made on anything, on Sky, Clear or anything," TVNZ spokesman Alastair Carthew said.
Clear chief executive Andrew Makin said he could not comment on shareholder matters.
TVNZ owns 25 percent of Clear and 16.4 percent of Sky. The Independent said the state-owned network had made no secret of its desire to increase the Sky stake.
Its opportunity came last year when Independent Newspapers Ltd, controlled by media mogul Rupert Murdoch, announced it was in negotiations to buy up to 83 percent of Sky from current shareholders.
An agreement between Sky's shareholders meant existing owners got first option to buy any shares up for sale and TVNZ made it clear it wanted to take up this option.

The Independent said the network believed that unless it expanded into pay-tv its share of the broadcasting market would gradually shrink. This would hit profits, dividends and the potential sale price should the government ever opt for privatisation, TVNZ argues.
However, the amount of money involved in any Sky expansion means TVNZ needs government approval, and this has not yet been given.
Because they are private companies, the respective values of Sky and Clear have not been made public, even in TVNZ's annual report.
But net of debt, Sky is estimated to be worth NZ$600 million, meaning every extra one percent TVNZ bought would cost about $6 million.

TVNZ has declined to say how much more of Sky it is after, but an informed source of the Independent's said that to gain sufficient say in the running of Sky, TVNZ would have to own between 25 and 33 percent.
